notes: Every write goes through config::set(section, key, value): the line Key=Value replaced (or added, the section too) in %LOCALAPPDATA%\RDRVR\RDRVR.user.ini, which overrides the game folder's RDRVR.ini. Section and key names match case-insensitively on read; the menu writes them with the case shown here.
Booleans are read by config::get_bool as true when the value is 1, true, yes or on (any case); the menu always writes 1 / 0 unless an item says otherwise.

default = the value in the released RDRVR.ini (config/RDRVR.ini with the release profile of tools/public/make_public.py, PROFILE_USER, on top: PROFILE_USER wins). Where the repo ini differs, repo_ini_default gives its value. Where neither ini has the key, the code default is given and default_source says code.
Vectors are one key holding space-separated numbers; components lists each part in order, written with the printf format in written.
restart: true only where the menu labels the row (restart) or the value is read at start; restart_note explains partial cases.
requires: the condition under which the row is enabled (the menu's sub_begin / BeginDisabled) or shown (shown_when).

items.label: Anti-aliasing
items.restart_note: Off, FXAA and Native TAA apply live (render_settings::set_aa) unless DLSS is running this start; switching to or from DLSS (3) applies at the next start. The menu shows a value below 0 as FXAA and above 3 as DLSS; -1 (the game's own) is ini only.
items.help: How edges are smoothed. FXAA is the default; Native TAA is the game's own. DLSS (NVIDIA RTX cards) is the sharpest; switching to or from it needs a restart.

items.label: Rendering (restart)
items.note: The menu reads any value but 0 as single pass (config::get_string("Stereo", "SinglePass", "1") == "0": two-pass) and writes 1 or 0 only. Under it a note says what runs now (config::single_pass_state, the converter's progress). The launcher's Graphics tab has the same switch (its Single pass row, which also puts back the stack's keys an older launcher wrote off).
items.help: Single pass draws both eyes from one walk of the scene, about a millisecond a frame faster; the shaders it needs are converted from your own game files in the background at the first start. Two-pass draws each eye on its own.

items.label: DLSS quality (restart)
items.requires: shown only when ForceAntiAliasing=3 (indented under it)
items.help: How much DLSS renders before it upscales. DLAA (native) is the sharpest and costs the most; the others are faster and softer.

items.label: Sharpening
items.help: Sharpens each eye's image in the headset (AMD CAS), bringing back detail DLSS and TAA soften. 0 = off.

items.label: Eyes in the headset's shape
items.restart_note: Turned on now it applies partly at once and fully after a restart (the eye images are sized when the headset session starts). If the game build has no hook for it, turning it on writes nothing.
items.help: Each eye drawn in your headset's own shape instead of a stretched 16:9 frame: fewer pixels for the same sharpness. With FXAA only. Turned on now, it fully applies after a restart.

items.label: Eyes in the headset's shape with DLSS (restart)
items.note: Ticking it also writes [XR] EyeShape=1; unticking writes only EyeShapeDlss=0 (EyeShape stays). Unticking the FXAA row above (EyeShape) clears this row's shown tick for the session without writing EyeShapeDlss.
items.help: The same with DLSS: each eye drawn smaller in the headset's shape, then upscaled by DLSS. About a quarter less GPU time for the same sharpness.

items.label: Motion blur
items.help: The game's motion blur. It smears the view as you turn your head, so it is off by default. On: the game's own graphics setting decides.

items.label: Heat haze
items.help: The desert's heat shimmer. Some find it uncomfortable in VR.

items.label: Render resolution: headset + Render resolution: size
items.note: Two combos. Headset list (index order): 0 'The game's own (its Graphics menu)', 1 'Automatic: what the headset asks for', then each headset as '<name> (eyes <h> tall)'. Size list (100% / 150% / 200%), enabled only for Automatic or a headset; labels '<pct>%: <W> x <H>' for a headset, '<pct>% of what the headset asks for' for Automatic. Picking a headset keeps the scale already picked when that size is allowed, else 100%; picking 'The game's own' forces 100%. Every pick writes all three keys: RenderHeadset = off | auto | <headset key>; RenderScale = 100 | 150 | 200 (100 for off); RenderResolution = off | auto | <H> (the height only, as a decimal string) for a headset, where H = 2*round(h*sqrt(pct/100)/2) and W = 2*round(H*8/9); if that size is out of range (640x480 to 9998x5624) RenderResolution=off. A headset or scale is disabled (not selectable) when the size needs more than 35% of the GPU's dedicated VRAM at 225 bytes per pixel, or the GPU has under 2560 MB; Automatic is always selectable. Automatic at run time: H = ceil(runtime's recommended height * [XR] EyeScale (if 0.25<x<4, else 1) * sqrt(pct/100)), capped at [Render] AutoMaxHeight when that is >= 480, rounded up to even, never below the game's own height; this the launcher need not compute (it writes auto). A RenderResolution written by hand (a height not in the table, or WxH 16:9) is shown as 'Custom (the ini's RenderResolution)' and the size combo is disabled; the mod reads RenderResolution first and uses RenderHeadset/RenderScale only when they give exactly that size (or for Automatic's scale).
items.help: The size the game renders at, matched to your headset. Automatic uses the size your VR runtime (SteamVR, Pimax Play, Virtual Desktop...) asks for. Windowed mode keeps the window's size. / Size: 100% is your headset's own resolution; 150% and 200% render more pixels (each side about 1.22 and 1.41 times) for a sharper picture at a higher cost.

items.label: Preset: Quality / Balanced / Performance
items.restart_note: The eye shape, DLSS and the resolution cap apply from the next start; the refresh rate at once.
items.note: Three buttons; none writes ForceAntiAliasing or the resolution keys. Every preset writes: XR.EyeShape=1 (via eye_shape::set_enabled, only if the build has the hook, and again via the DLSS row's setter), XR.EyeShapeDlss=1, Stereo.Split_shadows=1. Then Quality: Render.DlssQuality=0, Render.AutoMaxHeight=0, XR.EyeScale=1.0, XR.RefreshRate=0 (the runtime's). Balanced: Render.DlssQuality=5, Render.AutoMaxHeight=2880, XR.EyeScale=1.0, XR.RefreshRate=0. Performance: Render.DlssQuality=3, Render.AutoMaxHeight=2208, XR.EyeScale=0.85 if ForceAntiAliasing is not 3 else 1.0, XR.RefreshRate=72 only if the runtime offers a rate within 0.5 Hz of 72 (written %.0f of that rate), else RefreshRate untouched.
items.help: Quality: The sharpest: eyes in the headset's shape, DLSS at DLAA, the runtime's full size and refresh rate. For a fast PC. / Balanced: Eyes in the headset's shape, DLSS Quality, at most 2880 pixels tall. For most PCs. / Performance: Eyes in the headset's shape, DLSS Performance (without DLSS: 85% size), at most 2208 tall, 72 Hz where offered. For a slower PC.

items.label: Headset refresh rate
items.requires: shown only when the OpenXR runtime supports XR_FB_display_refresh_rate and lists rates (else a note: set it in the headset's or runtime's own settings)
items.note: Radio buttons: 'The runtime's' writes RefreshRate=0; then one radio per rate the runtime offers, labelled '<rate %.0f> Hz', writing the rate printed %.0f (e.g. 72, 90, 120). The mod uses the nearest offered rate. The list is known only at run time; a launcher can offer a number (0 = the runtime's).
items.help: Lower rates are easier on your PC. A frame that misses the rate halves it (90 to 45), so 72 or 80 can feel smoother on a slower PC. The runtime's: as your headset is set.

items.label: HUD on the left wrist
items.help: The radar and the ammo counter on the back of your left hand (the right when left-handed), shown when you look at it like a watch. Prompts stay on the floating screen.

items.label: What goes to the wrist
items.help: What goes to the wrist. The radar and ammo count only: anything else in that corner, such as a subtitle, stays on the floating screen. The whole corner: the screen's lower-left corner as a rectangle.

items.label: A double tap of Y at the wrist opens the satchel
items.help: With the wrist HUD in view, two quick presses of Y open John's satchel; B closes it. A single press still reaches the game, a third of a second late. Holding Y opens this menu either way.

items.label: Cutscenes
items.help: On the cinema screen: Cutscenes on a floating cinema screen, as the game frames them. / In 3D: Cutscenes all around you in 3D, seen from the cutscene's camera; your head only turns the view.

items.label: 3D separation
items.help: How strong the 3D is: 1.00 matches your own eyes, lower is flatter (a press 0.05).

items.label: Short scenes in first person
items.help: Short scripted moments (looting, skinning, doors, chests, beds, a mission's quick shots) stay at John's eyes instead of cutting to third person. Full cutscenes still follow the choice above. Needs First person.

items.label: Sound follows your head
items.help: Sounds are placed around your head as you turn it, so you can tell where they come from. Off: around the way John faces.

items.label: Sounds behind you at full volume
items.help: On stereo headphones the game plays sounds behind you much quieter (about 10 dB), so people behind you seem far away. On: they are as loud as in front. Surround (5.1 / 7.1) devices keep the game's mix.

items.label: Recentre
items.note: camera_lever::recentre(): the view, John's facing, the cinema screen and the HUD put in front of you again. Writes nothing; in-game only (also the headset's own recentre, Scroll Lock, or both stick clicks held a second).
items.help: Puts the view, John's facing, the cinema screen and the HUD in front of you again. Also: your headset's own recentre, or both stick clicks held a second.

items.label: First person
items.help: The view from John's eyes, moved by your head. Off: the game's own camera, turned by your head.

items.label: Eye height
items.help: Raises or lowers your view above John's eyes (a press 1 cm).

items.label: World scale
items.help: How big the world looks: above 1 bigger (you feel smaller), below 1 smaller. 1.00 is true scale. Only your view and hands change: the game's world, aiming and holsters stay the same (a press 0.05).

items.label: Room-scale walking
items.help: Step in your room and John walks under you, so your view moves only with your head. He turns to face your step, walks (never runs) and is put right under you at the end; your own stick always wins. Where he cannot follow (a wall, a fence, someone in the way) he stops and your view fades to black if you step on. On foot only: riding and cutscenes are as before. Mind ledges: a step toward one walks him off it.

items.label: Body moves with the headset
items.note: 2026-11-03 (round 73 check 8): moved here from the body rows.
items.help: John's body moves with you when you lean or step in your room, so it stays under your view; with room-scale walking, until he walks after you. Off: it stays where John stands.

items.label: Small steps at once
items.note: 2026-11-02, GOAL-older-items item 1 (a CAMERA_PROBE from his chest guards walls).
items.help: A small step (up to 20 cm) puts John right under you at once, without turning or walking, where nothing is in the way; longer steps, or with a wall between, he walks as before.

items.label: Step before he walks
items.note: pose::set_room_tuning writes RoomScaleDeadZone, RoomScaleStopRadius (0.06 as set; used at most 0.04 under the dead zone, 0.02 at the least), RoomScaleMinStick (0.38), RoomScaleMaxStick and RoomScaleMaxOffset (0.65) together, with their current values. RoomScaleLeanSlack (0.02) and RoomScaleStartLead (0.25) are ini-only.
items.help: How far you can move from John before he walks after you; inside it your view simply follows your head. A step already moving away starts him a little sooner (a press 5 cm).

items.label: His walking pace
items.note: Also writes the other RoomScale* tuning keys (their current values).
items.help: How hard the walk pushes the stick at most: 45% is the game's walk (a press 5%). Higher catches up sooner.

items.label: Fade out when he is blocked
items.help: Your view fades to black as you step past where John stopped (a wall, a fence, someone in the way), instead of passing through it. Off: the view is held 65 cm from him.

items.label: John turns when you turn
items.note: pose::set_body_follows_turn; BodyTurnGain (12), BodyTurnEaseS (0.08) and BodyTurnDuringWalk (1) are ini-only.
items.help: Turn your body in your room and John turns with you, smoothly, so he faces where you face; your view does not move with it. A look to the side does not turn him: only a turn past the angle below, held for the time below. Not while riding, in cover, in a menu or the wheel, or with a long gun held in both hands.

items.label: Turn past
items.note: pose::set_body_turn_tuning writes BodyTurnDeadZone, BodyTurnHoldMs and BodyTurnSpeed together, with their current values.
items.help: How far your head may turn from John's body before he turns after you: a look to the side inside it never turns him (a press 5 degrees).

items.label: Hold the turn
items.note: Also writes BodyTurnDeadZone and BodyTurnSpeed (their current values).
items.help: How long your head must stay turned past that angle before he follows: longer tells a glance aside from a turn more surely, shorter follows sooner (a press 50 ms).

items.label: His turn speed
items.note: Also writes BodyTurnDeadZone and BodyTurnHoldMs (their current values).
items.help: How fast he turns at most; he slows as he comes round to face you (a press 30 degrees a second).

items.label: Physical crouch
items.help: Crouch for real and John crouches; stand up and he stands. Your view follows your own head while you crouch. A look at the ground or a bend is not a crouch. Not while riding, in cover or in a menu. Sitting down counts as a crouch: when you sit, stand John up first (L3), then press "Set my standing height" seated (a recentre keeps the standing one). The left stick click still crouches too, and both stick clicks (the recentre) no longer crouch John on foot.

items.label: Crouch depth
items.note: pose::set_crouch_share also writes StandShare (kept at least 0.04 under it, default 0.18).
items.help: How far your head must drop to crouch John, as a share of your standing height (a press 5%). You stand him up again a little above it.

items.label: Crouch hold
items.note: pose::set_crouch_hold writes CrouchHoldMs alone. CrouchQuickHoldMs (50: the hold at 40 % past the depth) is ini-only.
items.help: How long your head must stay past the depth before John crouches (or back up before he stands): a quick dip or a nod does nothing. The further past the depth, the sooner: a quick, deep duck crouches him (a press 25 ms).

items.label: Set my standing height
items.note: pose::calibrate_standing(3000): the standing reference (and, with the headset's STAGE space, the standing eye height) taken after a 3 s countdown; refused while the game says John is crouched (the menu says to stand him first), dropped after 10 s without tracking. Writes nothing; in-game only (a recentre made standing takes it too).
items.help: Press, then stand straight and look ahead for 3 seconds: your crouch is measured from there (seated: sit and look ahead). Not while John is crouched: stand him up (L3) first. A recentre while standing sets it too.

items.label: Turning
items.help: Smooth turning: The right stick turns you smoothly, at the turn speed. / Snap turning: The right stick turns you in steps of the snap angle.

items.label: Turn speed
items.help: How fast smooth turning turns you at full tilt (a press 10).

items.label: Snap angle
items.help: How far each snap turns you (a press 5 degrees).

items.label: Snap turns in third person
items.help: With First person off, the right stick turns the view in one step at once while the game's camera catches up underneath. Not while aiming or on a mounted gun.

items.label: Third person snap angle
items.help: How far each third person snap turns the view (a press 5 degrees).

items.label: Steering
items.help: Steer with the stick: The view faces the horse and the left stick steers it; you can look around freely. / Steer with the head: As on foot: the left stick rides where you look.

items.label: The right stick turns the view while riding
items.help: The right stick turns your view as on foot while the left stick steers. Mounting or a recentre faces the horse again.

items.label: Recentre on getting on
items.note: 2026-11-02, GOAL-older-items item 25, after optimumbox's 0.8.11.11 (1.2 s after getting on).
items.help: Getting on a horse, onto a wagon or into a vehicle recentres your view (as holding both stick clicks): you face the mount's forward.

items.label: View from the saddle
items.note: pose::set_saddle writes SaddleAnchor and SaddleSmoothing (%.2f, its current value) together.
items.help: A steady view above the saddle instead of John's bouncing head.

items.label: Keep its height on climbs
items.help: On a steep climb the view keeps its height instead of sinking toward the saddle.

items.label: Saddle smoothing
items.note: Also writes SaddleAnchor (its current value). The code accepts 0..1.
items.help: How much the view's height is smoothed (0 = none; a press 0.05 s).

items.label: Left stick click brakes
items.help: On a horse or a wagon, hold the left stick click to slow down (with the stick pulled back for a hard stop). On foot it is still crouch.

items.label: Shown:
items.default_note: PROFILE_085 had arms; PROFILE_USER (which wins) has full, as does the repo ini.
items.help: How much of John you see in first person.

items.label: Forearms and hands when crouching, in cover or riding
items.help: Only the forearms and hands are drawn while crouching, in cover, riding or driving, where the body gets in the way.

items.label: The hidden body casts a shadow
items.help: With part of John hidden by "Shown" (forearms and hands, or hands only): his whole body's shadow on the ground. Off: no shadow of him at all.

items.label: The view at John's head where the game seats him
items.help: At a table game (poker, liar's dice, blackjack, five finger fillet, arm wrestling, horseshoes) and on a train's seat: the view at John's head as the game places him, instead of the standing eye height. Try it if his body shows in front of you.

items.label: John's own arms at the other table games
items.help: At horseshoes, five finger fillet and arm wrestling: John's arms as the game animates them (the knife and the horseshoe are in his animated hands), not on your controllers; you only press the game's buttons. Liar's dice, blackjack and poker keep your hands.

items.label: Hide head and hat
items.help: John's head and hat hidden in first person (cutscenes still show them).

items.label: Torso:
items.help: John's torso: upright over the hips, held still under your view (only the arms and legs move), only its lean removed, or as the game animates it.

items.label: Torso pitch
items.requires: enabled only when Stance=upright or Stance=still
items.help: Leans the upright torso forward (positive) or back.

items.label: Body back
items.help: Draws the body further behind your view, so looking down shows the chest rather than the inside (a press 1 cm).

items.label: Keep the torso over the hips
items.help: Running no longer pushes John's upper body forward into your view.

items.label: Lock body facing
items.help: The body, legs too, faces where you face: walking sideways no longer turns his shoulder into view.

items.label: Arms stretch to reach the controllers
items.requires: enabled only when [Hands] ArmIK=1 (Advanced tab, Arms follow the controllers)
items.help: Past John's reach his arm lengthens so his hand stays on your controller.

items.label: Longest arm
items.requires: enabled only when ArmIK=1 and ArmStretch=1
items.help: How far an arm may stretch, times its length; past it the hand stops short of the controller.

items.label: Wrist offset
items.help: How far John's wrist sits behind your controller's grip (a press 5 mm).

items.label: Hand pitch
items.help: Turns John's hand against your controller until it sits as yours does (degrees, a press 2; the left hand mirrored).

items.label: Hand yaw
items.help: Turns John's hand against your controller until it sits as yours does (degrees, a press 2; the left hand mirrored).

items.label: Hand roll
items.help: Turns John's hand against your controller until it sits as yours does (degrees, a press 2; the left hand mirrored).

items.label: Controller fit: your controller (a press 5 mm or 2 deg)
Controller fit (Offset right/up/forward, Pitch, Yaw, Roll)
items.requires: shown only once a controller has been seen (else 'No controller seen yet.'); edits only the key of the right controller's type in use
items.note: Controls.GripFit<Type> = 'right up forward pitch yaw roll' for the type in use (the right hand's; the left mirrored). A launcher cannot know the type in use; it can offer each type's key.
items.help: How this kind of controller sits in your hand: John's hands moved and turned from where the controller puts them (the left mirrored).

items.label: Where your hands grab (a press 5 mm)
Interaction spot
items.range_note: The arrows allow +-1.0; the setter clamps each part to +-0.25.
items.help: The point of your hand that grabs holsters, rounds, rings and a gun's parts (the dot Show the hand dots draws), moved from the wrist.

items.label: Body holsters
items.help: Reach to a holster and grip to draw its weapon; grip and let go there with the weapon to put it away. A buzz tells you a hand is at one.

items.label: Weapons by:
items.help: Draw by reaching to the holsters, or hold a grip to open the game's weapon wheel, move toward a weapon and let go (the holsters then draw nothing; the chest still gives rounds).

items.label: The wheel's hand: its stick is the D-pad
items.requires: enabled only when Holsters.Enabled=1 and Mode=wheel
items.help: While a grip holds the wheel open, push that hand's stick left or right to pick another gun of the highlighted kind (the game's D-pad); the stick neither walks nor turns meanwhile.

items.label: The world stands still while the wheel is open
items.requires: enabled only when Holsters.Enabled=1 and Mode=wheel
items.help: While a grip holds the weapon wheel open, the world nearly stops (the game's own time warp, as Dead Eye's) until you let go; it runs on at once after. Not while Dead Eye is on or a hand holds an object.

items.label: The world's speed meanwhile
items.requires: enabled only when Holsters.Enabled=1, Mode=wheel and WheelPause=1
items.help: How fast the world runs while the wheel is open: 0.02 is nearly still, 0.08 slow motion (a press 0.01; never 0).

items.label: Putting a gun away selects the fists
items.help: As the game's weapon wheel does: the left trigger then raises your fists instead of drawing the last gun.

items.label: Hold the grip to keep the gun
items.requires: enabled only when Holsters.Enabled=1 and Mode=holsters
items.help: Grip at a holster to draw and keep holding: the gun stays in your hand only while you hold the grip. Let go anywhere and it goes back in its holster; with your other hand on a long gun's foregrip, letting go leaves the gun carried by that hand (Carry a long gun by its foregrip). A second gun (dual wield) too. With a gun in hand your gun hand's grip is not the game's button (RB: the cover), except in Dead Eye (its paint). Not with the weapon wheel.

items.label: Draw into the hand that grabs the holster
items.help: The gun goes into whichever hand grabbed the holster, and that hand's trigger fires.

items.label: They follow:
items.help: Whether the holsters stay with John's body or move with you when you step around your room. Riding and cover always use the body.

items.label: Turn with the headset
items.requires: enabled only when Enabled=1 and Anchor=headset
items.help: The holsters turn around you as you turn your head. Off: they face the way John faces.

items.label: Turn by your head and hands
items.requires: enabled only when Enabled=1, Anchor=headset and TurnWithHead=1
items.help: While both hands aim in front of you, the holsters turn halfway toward your hands, so looking aside swings them less.

items.label: Turn dead zone
items.requires: enabled only when Enabled=1, Anchor=headset and TurnWithHead=1
items.help: How far you can look aside before the holsters follow: 0 follows every look; 30 to 45 lets you glance aside.

items.label: Steady when you lean
items.requires: enabled only when Enabled=1 and Anchor=headset
items.help: Leaning or bending over leaves the holsters at your hips; crouching and stepping still move them.

items.label: Placing: Off / Rings / Belt pieces and guns
items.note: Three radios, a session mode (in-game hand placing; nothing drawn while on). Off and Rings write nothing. 'Belt pieces and guns' also turns on Customize John's belt: writes Holsters.OwnBelt=1 and, with RingsFollowHolsters=1, re-saves each linked ring's <Key>Offset/<Key>Radius moved with its piece. The launcher should skip this.
items.help: Rings: close the menu, grip a holster's ring and move it. Belt pieces and guns: grip a piece of John's belt or a holstered gun, then move and turn it. Let go to leave it (saved). Nothing is drawn meanwhile: set Off when done.

items.label: Rings stay on their holsters
items.help: A holster's ring and its piece of John's belt keep their places to each other: moving one moves the other the same way. Off: each moves on its own. The ammo ring is always on its own.

items.label: Interaction points:
items.help: Rings: the rings below, as their switches say. Highlights: instead of the rings, a soft glow over the place itself (the gun's part, or the holster), only while using it would do something now (a holster with a gun to draw or room to put one away, the loading gate with room in the gun, the hammer when it can be cocked): what the gun needs at any distance, brighter within reach, the foregrip and a holster while a hand is near; never over your sights. Both: the rings and the highlights. Glowing parts: as highlights, but the gun's parts (the hammer, the lever, the bolt, the slide, the loading gate, the foregrip) glow on the gun itself, as if their own texture glowed, hidden where your hand covers them; the holsters have no glow.

items.label: The glow's colour
items.note: Three numbers, red green blue, each 0 to 1 (the menu's arrows: a press 0.05, written %.2f %.2f %.2f).
items.help: The glowing parts' colour (red, green, blue, each 0 to 1; a press 0.05). Round 45's warm gold is 1.00 0.84 0.52.

items.label: The glow's strength
items.help: How bright the glowing parts are against their own texture (0 to 8; 1 the default; a press 0.1).

items.label: Show the holsters
items.note: Also writes ShowHandDots and ShowWeaponPoints at their current values (so they stop following ShowZones at the next start).
items.help: Each holster as a ring, to place and size them: white, green with a hand in it, amber gripped.

items.label: Only near a hand
items.help: A ring shows, faintly, only while a hand comes near it.

items.label: Show the hand dots
items.help: A dot at each hand's grab point, green while it is in a holster or on the foregrip.

items.label: Show the weapon points
items.help: Where a gun takes your other hand: the foregrip ring, where a round goes in, and hints for working the action.

items.label: Show the guns at their holsters
items.help: Each holstered gun drawn at its holster, hidden while it is in a hand. Set each one's angle and place below.

items.label: The long guns on the back too
items.help: Off: only the hips' guns are shown.

items.label: Choose the weapon in each holster
items.help: Each holster draws the weapon you pick for it below (the game's weapon wheel follows). Automatic: the game's weapon for that slot.

items.label: Any weapon in the gun holsters
items.help: The hip and back holsters take any weapon you own, such as a pistol on the back. Put one away at a holster and it is drawn from there again. The knife, satchel and lasso holsters keep their own.

items.label: Customize John's belt
items.note: holster::set_own_pieces_linked: with RingsFollowHolsters=1, turning it on or off also moves each ring on a belt piece by that piece's move to or from the game's place and re-saves its <Key>Offset (LeftHip: LeftHipRingOffset while the mirrored holster is drawn) and <Key>Radius.
items.help: Move and turn John's holster, knife sheath, satchel, lasso and rifle sling (each holster below), and add a mirrored holster at the left hip. Off: the game's own belt; your places are kept.

items.label: A mirrored holster at the left hip
items.help: John's holster drawn again at the left hip for the secondary sidearm.

items.label: The knife, satchel and lasso on every outfit

items.note: 2026-10-29, GOAL-weapons-handling item 4. The cock by the other gun needs ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock.

With manual cocking, the other gun swept back across a single action's hammer cocks it. Looks only: your shots still go where the barrel points. A hand holding a round, a magazine, the foregrip or a part is never pushed off it.

items.label: Items in the free hand
items.note: 2026-10-29, off-hand items stages A (the knife), B (the throwables) and C (the torch; drawn unlit unless 'The free hand's torch lit').
items.help: With a gun in one hand, grip at the knife's sheath or the satchel with the other hand to draw the knife, the torch or a throwable into it: the gun stays in hand and keeps aiming, shooting and reloading. A fast stab or slash into someone hits as the game's knife; a fast swing of the torch knocks them and sets them alight; a slow move does neither. Let go of a throwable during a throw and it flies with your hand's speed; let go slowly, or of the knife or the torch, and it goes back where it came from.

It needs the torch to be one of your weapons the game has ready (choosing the torch on the weapon wheel may do it: not yet tried); otherwise it stays unlit. Needs "Items in the free hand" (and the launcher's "Flames follow the item in your hand", on unless you turned it off).

items.help: The Gatling, the Browning and the cannon: first person kept, John's hands on the gun, and the gun turned toward where your gun hand points (it learns the gun's barrel from your first shot). Off: the game's own camera and aim while you use one.

Off: the game's way (the right trigger places the X's, the duel fires them). Needs the right stick's flick up on.

items.note: Launcher only: not a row of menu.cpp, whose "The free hand's torch lit" names it ("the launcher's 'Flames follow the item in your hand', on unless you turned it off"). Read at the game's start ([Hands] HeldEffectsFollow, anchors IdleFxMatrixRet).

items.label: Dual wield
items.help: With a gun in one hand, grip another gun holster with the free hand to take a second gun, with its own trigger and ammo.

items.label: The knife beside a gun is the game's knife
items.requires: enabled only when DualWield=1 (indented under it)
items.help: Your other hand draws the knife while a gun is in hand: the knife becomes the game's own weapon in that hand (its stab hits as the game's knife) and the gun the second gun in your gun hand. Off: the knife as a copy beside the gun.

items.label: A gun beside the torch
items.requires: enabled only when DualWield=1 (indented under it)
items.note: 2026-10-29 (the user: the torch lit in one hand, a working gun in the other; research/run28/torch_second_gun.md). Exactly the torch (eWeapon 33, Undead Nightmare) as the game's weapon in hand; not the copy, and no cross reload beside it.
items.help: Undead Nightmare: with the torch in one hand (lit, as the game's weapon), grip a gun holster with the free hand to take a second gun, as beside a gun: its own trigger, reticle and ammo. Press it to your chest for one round at a time (with the chest squeeze off it can't be reloaded beside the torch; the torch hand takes no rounds for it). Put the torch away and the second gun becomes the gun in hand.

items.label: Each hand reloads the other gun
items.requires: enabled only when DualWield=1 or DualWieldCopy=1
items.help: With a second gun or the copy out, grip at the chest with either hand to take rounds for the gun in your OTHER hand, then bring them to that gun's loading ring. Rounds per grab and one-at-a-time apply, as do its action's gates (a revolver in hand must be open; a second gun that opens to load takes none with the manual actions on, unless opened by its stick (below); the copy has no action of its own and always takes them, or with that option only while open). The hand holding rounds does not fire its own gun until they are in and its trigger is let go. The chest squeeze is off for the two guns while this is on.

items.label: Open the second gun by its stick
items.requires: enabled only when DualWield=1 or DualWieldCopy=1
items.note: 2026-10-28, round 37 check 4. Acts only with [Reload] ManualActions=1 and a revolver (ManualRevolver) as the second gun or the copy, in the layout's left-stick hand. With it on, the gates of 'Each hand reloads the other gun' let such a second gun (and the copy) take rounds only while it is open.
items.help: With each gun's action by hand on and a revolver as the second gun or the copy: hold that hand's stick down and click it to open the gun (its rounds then go in, with the option above), and flick that hand (a roll or a turn) to shut it, as the gun in your gun hand. That click never crouches or brakes. While such a gun is out, a quick flick of that stick back does not walk you back (on foot; riding, the stick slows the horse at once as before) and a quick click does nothing: hold the stick back, or the click in, a moment longer (the two waits below) to walk back, crouch, or brake on a horse. While it is open its trigger does nothing; Dead Eye shuts it. With revolvers cocked by a flick, a single action there needs that stick's quick flick down after each shot, as the gun in hand does.

items.label: The walk back waits
items.requires: enabled only when (DualWield=1 or DualWieldCopy=1) and DualWieldOpen=1
items.note: 2026-10-29 (the user: a quick flick or click should not walk back, crouch or brake). Acts only while the open gesture is armed (the option on, a second gun that opens out on the left stick's hand, not carried); the stick held at the middle that long once it is pulled back into the open cone.
items.help: While the second gun can be opened by its stick, on foot: how long that stick pulled back waits before you walk back, so a quick flick down to open the gun does not move you. Riding, there is no wait.

items.label: The click held in for
items.requires: enabled only when (DualWield=1 or DualWieldCopy=1) and DualWieldOpen=1
items.note: 2026-10-29. Acts only while the open gesture is armed; the click passes at once when the right stick's click is already down (the recentre chord), and PhysicalCrouch's 150 ms chord wait is not added on top.
items.help: While the second gun can be opened by its stick: how long that stick's click must be held in before it crouches you (or brakes on a horse). A quicker click does nothing.

items.label: The same sidearm in both hands
items.help: With a sidearm in hand, grip a hip holster with the free hand to take a copy of it; let go at a hip to put it back.

items.label: The copy drawn as a prop
items.help: Draws the copy as a model of the gun, so you see it in the free hand.

items.label: Your other sidearm's model
items.help: If you own a different sidearm, the copy is that gun (the hip holster's), and its shots leave its muzzle.

items.label: A second of the gun at its own holster
items.requires: enabled only when DualWieldCopy=1 and DualWieldOwnModel=1
items.help: Gripping the holster the gun was drawn from gives a second of that same gun; the other hip still gives your other sidearm.

items.label: The copy hits as the gun it shows
items.requires: enabled only when DualWieldCopy=1 and DualWieldOwnModel=1
items.help: The copy's shots do the damage of the gun it shows (the other sidearm's), not the gun in hand's. Takes effect from the next start of the game.

items.label: Two-handed long guns
items.help: Grip a long gun's foregrip with your other hand, ahead of the gun hand, to aim it with both hands.

items.label: The front hand snaps onto the gun
items.help: While you hold the foregrip, John's front hand sits on the gun as the game holds it, instead of following your controller.

items.label: The front hand turns the gun
items.help: On: the gun points from your gun hand toward your front hand. Off: John's front hand is drawn holding the gun, but only your gun hand moves it.

items.label: Physical rifle stock
items.help: For a stock that holds both controllers: your front hand's trigger at the foregrip takes hold of the gun as its grip does (the trigger still aims), and only your gun hand aims the gun.

items.label: Calibrate the stock
items.note: Closes the menu; within 5 s the player holds a long gun on the stock aiming down the sights; the mod learns [Reload] StockTurn (a rotation vector in degrees, written %.2f %.2f %.2f). In-game only; the launcher should skip it. Enabled only when TwoHanded=1 and PhysicalStock=1; replaced by a countdown note while armed.
items.help: Press (the menu closes), then within 5 seconds hold any long gun on your stock with both hands, aiming down the sights: every long gun is set straight along the stock with its top up.

items.label: Clear the stock calibration
items.note: Writes [Reload] StockTurn=0.00 0.00 0.00 (repo/release default 0 0 0). Enabled only when TwoHanded=1 and PhysicalStock=1. A launcher can replicate it.
items.help: The long guns back to the game's own angle in your gun hand.

items.label: Carry a long gun by its foregrip
items.help: Holding a long gun with both hands, hold your gun hand's grip half a second away from the holsters, then let go (a quick tap stays the game's cover): the front hand keeps the gun by its foregrip (carried, it does not fire) and the gun hand is free to draw another weapon. Grip near the gun's grip with the empty hand to take it back; let go with the front hand to put it back in its holster.

items.label: This gun: <gun in hand> (a press 5 mm)
Its own settings; without its own it uses every gun's (the Reloading tab). Offsets right / up / forward along the gun.
This gun: The foregrip / The foregrip ring / The loading ring / The magazine / The action's spot (per gun, per hand)
items.requires: shown only with a weapon in hand (else the note 'Hold a gun to give it its own foregrip, rings and front-hand hold here; a gun without its own uses every gun's (the Reloading tab).'); for weapon_tokens index 0..37 (2026-11-01, C35: every weapon, the Blunderbuss and the Explosive Rifle too). The foregrip and foregrip ring rows only for the long guns (8-20, 31, 34); the magazine row only for the magazine pistols with [Reload] PistolMagazines on (SemiAutoPistol, HighPower, Mauser). A radio 'Right hand' / 'Left hand' (default Right) picks which hand's set the rows show and write.

components.label: Offset right / up / forward (each of the three)

items.range_note: The arrows allow offsets of +-1.0; the setter clamps them to +-0.4.
items.note: Three groups for the gun in hand. The foregrip (where John's front hand sits): ForegripOffset only. The foregrip ring: ForegripRingOffset + ForegripRingRadius (both written on any change). The loading ring: LoadPointOffset + LoadPointRadius. Each group's heading says '(its own)' or '(now every gun's)'; until set it shows and starts from every gun's value ([Reload] ForegripOffset / ForegripZoneOffset+ForegripZoneRadius / LoadPointOffset+LoadPointRadius). Each group's button 'Use every gun's' (enabled only when the gun has its own) writes the group's keys as empty values (Key=), which the mod reads as unset. (2026-11-01, C8, C8b, C38) Each hand its own: the Left hand radio writes the same keys with the suffix Left (unset: the right hand's). The magazine: MagazineWellOffset only (right / up / forward from the pistol's well, unset: 0 0 0, 'as made'). C8b: a change to the right hand's set while the left has none of its own first writes the left's current value (the right's, else every gun's) to the ...Left keys, so the left stays where it was. The action's spot (C36, every gun): PartOffset only (right / up / forward; unset 0 0 0, 'as made'), moving the zone where the other hand takes the action (the bolt's handle, the breech, the slide, the fanned hammer, the muzzle's ramrod); the drawn parts do not move.
items.default_note: These per-gun sections exist only in the release ini (make_public.py appends them); the repo ini has none.
items.help: The foregrip: Where John's front hand sits on this gun. / The foregrip ring: Where your front hand takes hold of this gun, and the ring's size. / The loading ring: Where a round goes into this gun, and the ring's size. / The magazine: Where this pistol's magazine goes in (its well under the grip). / The action's spot (bolt, breech, slide, hammer): Where your other hand takes this gun's action: the bolt's handle, the breech, the slide, the fanned hammer or the muzzle's ramrod. / Right hand: Set this gun's places for when your right hand holds it. / Left hand: Set this gun's places for when your left hand holds it (until you change them, it uses the right hand's). / Use every gun's: Clears this gun's own setting for this hand: it uses every gun's (the Reloading tab) again (the left hand: the right hand's).

items.label: The front hand's hold: (per long gun)
items.default_source: code (the release ini also sets Weapon.SawedOff, Weapon.PumpAction and Weapon.Carbine to aiming)
items.requires: shown only with a long gun in hand (weapon_tokens index 8..20: Carbine .. Carcano, and since round 67 31 the Explosive Rifle and 34 the Blunderbuss; the launcher's rows are 8..20 only); the '(... once first)' suffix shows until the game has shown that hold on the gun this session
items.help: Which of the game's holds John's front hand uses on this gun: the one for its stance (Automatic), or always the lowered or the aiming hold.

items.label: Reload by hand
items.help: Grip at your chest with the hand that has no gun to take a round (a buzz), and bring it to the open gun to load it. Not in Dead Eye.

items.label: Your empty hand's trigger takes a round
items.help: At the chest, your empty hand's trigger takes a round as its grip does; keep it pulled while you bring the round to the gun. The trigger still aims as usual.

items.label: Rounds taken at once
items.help: How many rounds a grip at your chest takes, as many as the gun has room for; all of them drawn in your hand.

items.label: The rounds held go in:
items.help: One at a time: held at the gun's loading ring, the rounds go in one after another. All at once: they all go in as they reach it. Let go at the gun, the rest go in.

items.label: Rounds come from:
items.help: Your chest: grip at your chest to take rounds. Grip near the gun: also grip with your empty hand near the gun's loading ring (within a hand's width of it), and the rounds appear in your hand; push them into the ring (gripped inside the ring, they go straight in). Palm up: also turn your empty hand palm up, away from the gun, and grip. When dual wielding, either hand takes rounds for the other gun. Gripping a part of the gun (a bolt, the barrels, the foregrip) still works that part.

items.label: Show the rounds at the chest
items.help: While the gun can take a round, a row of its rounds at your chest (up to six).

items.label: The gun hand squeezed at the chest:
items.help: Gripping at your chest with the gun hand: nothing, one round in, or a full reload.

items.label: The game's automatic reloads
items.help: The game's own reloads as well: after the last round, when drawing an empty gun, or on an empty trigger pull.

items.label: The game's reload button
items.help: The game's reload button works as well as the hand reload.

items.label: Rounds seen in the hand:
items.note: 2026-10-27: the menu's three radios (it was one checkbox, 2 ini only). 2: a shotgun's shells are the game's own model (p_gen_shellshotgun01x, loaded from the player's install), in the hand and in the row at the chest; the mod's own shell stands in until they are made.
items.help: Draws the rounds you took at the chest between your fingers (and the row at the chest). The game's shotgun shells: a shotgun's shells are the game's own model, in the hand and at the chest, lit by the game.

items.label: Each gun's own round (the new models)
items.help: Each gun's round at its real size, textured and lit as the game's own props. Off: the old simple rounds.

items.label: The round in your: Left hand / Right hand (Offset, Direction: Along the fingers / Out of the hand / Custom, Turn, Tilt, Brightness)

components.label: Tilt (degrees; wraps past 180 to -175, past 90 over the top)

items.note: (2026-10-31, R13) A radio 'Left hand' / 'Right hand' (default Left) picks the hand: the left hand's place is RoundOffset and RoundAxis (every hand's until the right has its own), the right hand's RoundOffsetRight and RoundAxisRight; RoundBrightness is shared. Any change writes the hand's two keys and RoundBrightness. RoundAxis: 'Along the fingers' writes 1.000 0.000 0.000; 'Out of the hand' writes auto; Custom (chosen by its radio or by moving Turn/Tilt) writes the unit vector (cos(tilt)*cos(turn), cos(tilt)*sin(turn), sin(tilt)) as %.3f %.3f %.3f. Turn and Tilt are shown from the current axis (turn = atan2(y, x), tilt = asin(z), rounded; the angles last set are kept while the axis is theirs) and 0 0 in Out of the hand.
items.help: Left hand: Set where the round sits in your left hand. / Right hand: Set where the round sits in your right hand (until you change it, it uses the left hand's place). / Offset: The round moved from between your thumb and index (a press 2 mm). / Direction: Which way the round points: along the fingers, out of the hand, or your own by the two angles. / Turn, Tilt: The round's direction as two angles from along the fingers (a press 5 degrees; each goes all the way round); either makes it Custom. / Brightness: How bright the drawn rounds are, in the hand and at the chest (a press 0.25).

items.label: A gun's own (the Guns tab, This gun) replace these. Offsets right / up / forward along the gun.
The foregrip: where John's front hand sits on the gun (Offset)
items.help: Where John's front hand sits on the gun.

items.label: The foregrip ring: where your front hand takes hold (Offset, Size)
items.help: Where your front hand takes hold of the gun, and the ring's size (Show the weapon points draws it); John's hand still sits at the foregrip.

items.label: The loading ring: where a round goes in (Offset, Size, A round goes in at a touch)

components.label: A round goes in at a touch

items.written: LoadPointOffset %.3f %.3f %.3f; LoadPointRadius %.3f; InsertOnTouch 1|0 (all three on any change)
items.help: Where a round goes into the gun in hand, and the ring's size: a round brought inside it goes in. / A round goes in at a touch: The round itself touching the ring loads it. Off: your wrist has to be inside the ring.

items.label: Work each gun's action by hand
items.help: Open a revolver with the right stick (as chosen under Revolvers) and close it with a flick of the gun; work a bolt, lever or pump by hand after each shot. The trigger waits until you do.

items.label: Revolvers drawn open
items.help: An open revolver is drawn open: the Schofield and LeMat tip down, the Double-action's cylinder swings out, the Cattleman's gate opens.

items.label: Revolvers:

options.label: Opened by a flick of the stick
Cocked by a flick, opened by holding it and clicking

items.help: Opened by a flick: a flick of the right stick down opens a revolver. Cocked by a flick: after each shot, a flick of the right stick down cocks the Cattleman's, the Schofield's and the LeMat's hammer (the Double-action needs none); hold the stick down and click it to open a revolver. Either way a flick of the gun shuts it. A revolver drawn into your other hand is worked by that hand's stick (on foot).

items.label: John's thumb cocks the hammer
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock
items.help: On the stick's flick, John's thumb reaches up to the hammer and draws it back, then returns to the grip. The shot is ready at the flick either way.

items.label: Fan the hammer with your other hand
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock
items.help: Sweep your other hand's palm back across the hammer to cock it; keep the trigger pulled and each sweep fires.

items.label: Fanning zone size
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock and FanHammer=1
items.help: How near the hammer your other hand's sweep must pass (a ball this far round it). Larger is easier to hit, and a resting hand fires sooner. 0.08 m by default.

items.label: Fanning speed
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock and FanHammer=1
items.help: How fast the sweep must be to cock the hammer. Lower is more sensitive. 1.0 m/s by default.

items.label: Show the fanning zone
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and RevolverControl=cock and FanHammer=1
items.help: A ring round the hammer as big as the zone: bright while a sweep would cock it, lit while your hand is in it, faint while your hand must leave it before the next sweep counts.

items.label: Lever guns: the lever drawn as you work it
items.help: The lever drawn opening and closing as you work it, with the game's lever sounds.

items.label: Lever guns:

options.label: Stick held, gun down and up

items.help: Stick held, gun down and up: hold the right stick down, move the gun down to open the lever and up to shut it; the gun stays put meanwhile. / Roll the gun: after a shot, roll your gun hand a little left or right to open the lever, and back to shut it. / Flick the stick: after a shot, a flick of the right stick down works the lever. / Flick the gun: after a shot, flick the gun down and back up (with the lever drawn: the flick down opens it, the flick up shuts it).

items.label: Roll to open
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and LeverControl=roll
items.help: How far the gun hand rolls (either way) to open the lever. Rolling back most of the way shuts it. 20 degrees by default.

items.label: Volcanic: its lever by a flick of the right stick
items.help: After each shot, a flick of the right stick down works the Volcanic's lever, whatever the lever guns use.

items.label: Pump-action: the fore-end in your front hand
items.help: After a shot, pull the fore-end back with your front hand (held two-handed) and push it forward.

items.label: Bolt actions: the bolt in your other hand
items.help: Bolt Action and Carcano: grip the bolt with your other hand, lift, pull back (rounds go in now), push forward and turn it down.

items.label: Bolt actions: the bolt by your gun hand when carried by the foregrip
items.help: With a bolt gun carried by its foregrip (Carry a long gun by its foregrip), your free gun hand works the bolt as your other hand does in hand. A shot not yet cycled goes with the gun and stays so until you work the bolt; grip near the gun's grip to take it back. The carried gun never fires.

items.label: Blunderbuss: the ramrod at your chest
items.help: After the round is down the barrel, take the ramrod at your chest with your other hand, bring it to the muzzle, push it in and pull it out: loaded. Off: your bare hand at the muzzle makes two ram strokes, as before.

items.label: Take the ramrod:
items.requires: shown only when ManualActions=1 and RamrodAtChest=1
items.note: Read as From the gun unless the value is chest.
items.help: From the gun: Grip it with your other hand where it lies under the Blunderbuss's barrel. / At your chest: Grip it at your chest with your other hand.

items.label: Where it is taken on the gun
items.requires: shown only when ManualActions=1, RamrodAtChest=1 and RamrodFrom=gun
items.help: The ramrod's grab point on the gun: right, up, forward along the gun (a press 5 mm).

items.label: The ramrod in your: Left hand / Right hand (The ramrod in the hand: Offset, Turn, Tilt)
items.requires: shown only when ManualActions=1 and RamrodAtChest=1
items.note: A radio 'Left hand' / 'Right hand' (default Left) picks the hand: the left hand's (and every hand's until the right has its own) RamrodOffset, RamrodTurn, RamrodTilt; the right hand's the same keys with the suffix Right. Any change writes the hand's three keys.
items.help: Left hand: Set where the ramrod sits in your left hand. / Right hand: Set where the ramrod sits in your right hand (until you change it, the left's). / Where the ramrod sits in your hand: right, up, forward along your hand (a press 5 mm), and its direction from where your hand points (a press 5 degrees).

items.label: Bolt actions: the bolt by the off hand's trigger
items.help: Work the bolt of the gun in your hand with your other hand's trigger (pull it at the bolt and make the strokes); that trigger does not aim while it is at the bolt. Off: by its grip, as before.

items.label: The carried bolt by the trigger
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and CarriedBolt=1
items.help: Work the carried gun's bolt with your gun hand's trigger (pull it at the bolt and make the strokes); your grip then always takes the gun back, even beside the bolt. Off: by the grip, as before (a grip nearer the gun's grip than its bolt takes it back).

items.label: Pump-action: pumped by a jerk when carried by the foregrip
items.help: With the Pump-action carried by its foregrip (Carry a long gun by its foregrip), snap that hand back along the barrel to pump it back, then forward to close it: a one-handed pump. A shot not yet pumped goes with the gun; grip near the gun's grip to take it back as you left it. The carried gun never fires.

items.label: Single-shot rifles opened by hand
items.help: Open the Springfield's trapdoor and the Rolling Block's block with your other hand (the Buffalo by a flick down and up), load one round, shut.

items.label: Semi-Auto Shotgun: the bolt racked by hand
items.help: After loading it from empty, pull back the bolt's handle (right of the receiver) with your other hand and let go.

items.label: Pistols: magazines (the Mauser: a stripper clip)
items.help: Semi-Automatic Pistol and High Power: flick the right stick down to drop the magazine (a round stays in the chamber if the gun wasn't empty; its rounds go back to your ammo). Take a new one with your other hand (at your chest, or as "Rounds come from" says) and push it up into the bottom of the grip: the gun is loaded. Mauser: pull its bolt back by the ears with your other hand (it stays open when empty), push a stripper clip down into the top, then pull the bolt and let go (or flick the stick down) to close it. No single rounds go into these three.

items.label: Magazine in the hand: Left hand / Right hand (Offset, Turn, Tilt; with a magazine pistol in hand, that pistol's own)
items.note: Shown only while PistolMagazines is on. (2026-10-31, R13; 2026-11-01, C38) A radio 'Left hand' / 'Right hand' (default Left) picks the hand. With no magazine pistol in hand the rows are every pistol's: the left hand's (and every hand's until the right has its own) MagazineOffset, MagazineTurn, MagazineTilt; the right hand's the same keys with the suffix Right. With a magazine pistol in hand (<Token> SemiAutoPistol, HighPower or Mauser) they are that pistol's own in [Weapon.<Token>]: HeldMagazineOffset, HeldMagazineTurn, HeldMagazineTilt for the right hand, the suffix Left for the left (unset: the hand's for every pistol). Any change writes the three keys of the set shown. Its button 'Use every pistol's' (with a pistol in hand, enabled when it has its own) writes that pistol's three keys for the hand as empty values.
items.requires: shown only when ManualActions=1 and PistolMagazines=1
items.help: Left hand: Set the magazine's place in your left hand. / Right hand: Set the magazine's place in your right hand (until you change it, the left hand's). / Where the magazine (the Mauser's clip) sits in your hand, apart from the rounds' place on the Reloading tab (a press 2 mm, or 5 degrees). Its fit into the gun follows it. With a pistol in hand: that pistol's. / Use every pistol's: Clears this pistol's own magazine place for this hand.

items.label: Pistols: the slide racked by hand
items.help: Semi-Automatic Pistol (its toggle), High Power and Mauser (its bolt): grip the slide with your other hand, pull it back and let go to chamber a round. Racking with a round already chambered throws it out (it is lost). After the last shot the slide stays back: put a new magazine in, then rack it. With nothing chambered the trigger does nothing.

items.label: Break actions opened by the stick
items.help: Double-barrel and Sawed-off: hold the right stick down and click it to open (with [Reload] BreakOpenClick=0 in the ini: a flick down); shut with a flick of the gun up, or swing the barrels up with your other hand.

items.label: John's hand on the barrels as they swing up
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and ManualBreak=1
items.help: While your other hand holds the open barrels, John's hand is drawn on them.

items.label: John's hand on the part your other hand grips
items.requires: enabled only when ManualActions=1 and (BoltParts=1 or BreechParts=1 or SemiAutoParts=1 or PistolSlides=1 or PistolMagazines=1)
items.help: While your other hand works a bolt or a breech, John's hand is drawn on it, moving with it.

items.label: A click when fired before the action is worked
items.help: A trigger pull before the gun is closed or worked plays the empty click.

items.label: An empty gun
items.help: What an empty gun's trigger does: a click from the gun's side, a controller buzz, both, or nothing.

items.label: Click volume
items.requires: enabled only when EmptyClick=sound or EmptyClick=both
items.note: Each press in the menu also plays one click at the new level.
items.help: The click's loudness, 0 to 1 (the game's volume settings do not change it; the Windows mixer does). Each press plays it once.

items.label: Throw by hand
items.help: Dynamite, fire bottles, throwing knives and tomahawks fly with your hand's speed and direction: pull the trigger and swing.

items.label: Throw strength
items.note: gestures::set_tuning writes SwingSpeed and ThrowGain together (%.2f each).
items.help: How hard throws fly, times your hand's speed (a press 0.1).

items.label: Throw by letting go of the grip
items.help: Hold your gun hand's grip, pull the trigger to light or ready the throwable, then swing and let go of the grip to throw. A lit one held too long goes off in your hand.

items.label: Melee by swing
items.help: A fast swing of either hand punches with the fists, stabs with the knife or strikes with the torch.

items.label: Lasso by hand
items.help: Throw the lasso with its trigger or a swing (as chosen below); yank back to pull on the rope.

items.label: Thrown by:
items.help: Trigger: The lasso hand's trigger throws it. / Swing: A fast swing toward where you aim throws it. / Either: A swing or the trigger. / Lock on: Hold the left trigger (LT, the game's aim) to lock on to the one you look at and spin the lasso; then the right trigger (RT) or a throwing swing throws it (not without the hold), the lasso in either hand. Let go without either: nothing thrown.
items.note: Lock on (lock, 2026-10-30) aims by the head whatever Aimed by says; the menu shows 'Lock on aims by your head (the choice below applies to the other ways).' under it.

items.label: Aimed by:
items.help: Head: Where you look. / Lasso hand: Where the lasso hand points. / Other hand: Where your other hand points: point at the target, throw with the lasso hand.

items.label: Swing speed
items.requires: enabled only when Melee=1 or Lasso=1
items.note: gestures::set_tuning writes SwingSpeed and ThrowGain together (%.2f each).
items.help: How fast a swing must be to punch or throw the lasso (a press 0.25 m/s).

items.label: Gun-butt melee
items.help: Hit someone by swinging the gun in your hand: the game's own melee blow, a knock-out by default, with its crime and anger.

items.label: Hit speed
items.help: How fast the swing must be to hit (a press 0.25 m/s).

items.label: Hit strength
items.help: How much of a person's knock-out a hit takes (100 knocks them down in one hit; a hard swing doubles it). The game's own: 10.

items.label: Whistle for the horse
items.help: A hand at your mouth and its trigger: John whistles for his horse. The gun hand whistles only with no gun in it.

items.label: Fists on both triggers
items.help: With nothing in your hands, hold both triggers for the fighting stance and swing a fist to punch while holding them; raise both fists before your face to block. A trigger alone does nothing. Off: each trigger as the game has it.

items.label: Guard with both fists
items.help: With your fists out, raise both hands before your face and hold both triggers to block. Fists raised without the triggers stay lowered for the game (raised fists alarm people).

items.label: Tip the hat to greet
items.help: Your right hand at your hat's brim and its trigger: John tips his hat and greets (the game's greet button).

items.label: Hands push loose objects (experimental)
items.help: An empty hand moving through a bottle, a crate or a chair pushes it. People are never pushed.

items.label: Grab loose objects (experimental)
items.help: Grip a loose prop with an empty hand to hold it; let go to throw it with your hand's speed. People are never grabbed.

items.label: Left-handed
items.note: Writes only LeftHanded (the button remap keys are not swapped; the mod swaps the controllers' roles itself).
items.help: Swaps the controllers: the left trigger fires and the right stick moves.

items.label: The trigger alone fires
items.help: The right trigger alone fires; the mod holds the game's aim button for you.

items.label: Aim while the gun is raised
items.help: Raising the gun in front of you holds the game's aim for you, so every pull fires at once.

items.label: Sprinting lowers the raised gun
items.help: The sprint button lowers a raised gun so John can run with it; a pull still fires.

items.label: Jumping lowers the raised gun
items.help: The jump button lowers a raised gun first, so John can jump, vault and climb with a gun in hand.

items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Left Y
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Left stick click
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Right stick click
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Left grip
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Right grip
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Left trigger
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Right trigger
items.help: The game button this VR button drives. A trigger set to a button presses it past halfway; a button set to LT or RT pulls it fully.

items.label: Reset to the game's scheme
items.note: Writes the ten keys back to RightA=A, RightB=B, LeftX=X, LeftY=Y, LeftStickClick=L3, RightStickClick=R3, LeftGrip=LB, RightGrip=RB, LeftTrigger=LT, RightTrigger=RT. A launcher can replicate it.
items.help: Every VR button back to the game button of its own name.

items.label: The menu: hold the menu button (without one: both B buttons), hold Y with the wrist HUD in view, or F7. A tap of the menu button pauses; held with the right stick it is the D-pad, with A the satchel. The right stick scrolls the menu.
These are on for a reason. Turn one off only to compare, or if it misbehaves for you.
Long guns held by their aiming grip
items.help: Each long gun held the way the game holds it when aiming, in every pose. Off: the game's own hold of each moment.

items.label: Sidearms held by their aiming grip
items.help: Each revolver or pistol held the way the game holds it aimed, so it moves with your hand at once. Off: the game's own hold, which can lag your hand when the game runs slowly.

items.label: Arms follow the controllers
items.help: John's arms reach to your controllers and his hands turn with them. Off: the game's own arm animation.

items.label: Shadows drawn once for both eyes
items.help: Shadows drawn once for both eyes instead of once per eye: about 0.9 ms faster a frame; a shadow's edge can shift by a pixel.

items.label: Steady gun far out
items.note: 2026-11-02, GOAL-older-items item 21, after optimumbox's 0.8.11.11 (cycle N14: 0.14/0.36 mm a frame to 0).
items.help: The gun in your hand doesn't tremble far from the map's middle (the game's positions there step by half a millimetre): held where it was while your hand and head stay still.

items.label: Still clothes
items.note: 2026-11-02, GOAL-older-items item 23, after optimumbox's 0.8.11.11.
items.help: John's clothes don't flutter in the wind (seen from inside the body it reads as a buzz).

items.label: Coat on the drawn body (test)
items.note: 2026-11-06 (GOAL-remaining item 2); the menu row 2026-11-10, round 122.
items.help: The duster's coat drawn on John's drawn body, each part with the body at its height (hips to chest), not swaying with the game's own walk and idle. Off: the whole coat moved with the hips.

items.label: Coat held still (test)
items.note: 2026-11-10, round 124: with ClothPins; the seconds the coat's points are eased over in the drawn hips' frame (the menu sets 1.00).
items.help: With the option above: the duster's coat hangs still on your body, the game's walking and idle sway smoothed out (it follows a slow change, a crouch or the saddle, in about a second). Off: the coat swings as the game simulates it.

items.label: Arm motion vectors (experimental)
items.help: Tells DLSS and TAA how John's arms moved, which may cut the ghosting beside fast-moving arms.

items.label: Show the launcher when the game starts (next start)
items.help: RDRVR_Launcher.exe opens on the desktop each time the game starts, and the game waits for its Play: the settings saved there apply to that start. Off: the game starts at once, as before.

items.label: Goes on by itself after
items.help: If nobody presses Play (you started the game from the headset), the game goes on after this many seconds with the saved settings. A click in the launcher stops the countdown; 0: no countdown (the game still goes on after 5 minutes). Applies at the next start.

ini_only_player.help: The game's rumble on the VR controllers.
Eye image height against the runtime's recommended one: below 1 faster, above 1 sharper (the Performance preset sets 0.85).
Automatic resolution at most this tall (the presets set 2880 / 2208).
Rain and blood drops on the lens (the game's screen overlay).
The game's soft lock and reticle magnet in first person.
1: the gun is in the hand at once; 0: the game's draw clip plays first.
Keep first person when a script switches to its own camera (shops, missions); try 0 if a mission scene looks wrong.
A gun drawn: the view's height held as standing, or lowered with the game's armed stance.
Driving a wagon or coach: the view faces and turns with the vehicle.
How long the menu button is held to open the RDRVR menu.
The wrist double tap's window (with WristSatchel=1).
In the game's menus RT/LT switch tabs and the left stick steps one item a push.

ini_only_player.values: empty | path to a 16-bit PCM WAV
ini_only_player.help: Your own empty-gun click for every weapon (also EmptyClickRevolver / EmptyClickRifle / EmptyClickShotgun per family, default RDRVR_click_<family>.wav).
With the hand reload: let the game switch weapons when the gun in hand is out of rounds.
Gun-butt melee: 0 knocks out, 1 takes health.
How fast the carrying hand must snap back and forward along the barrel to pump the carried Pump-action. Lower: easier, but a quick move of that hand may pump it.
